move.headline: A normal-sized fall, inside SpaceX's usual daily range

evidence.t: Shares were down 0.8% at $166.30 in US trading (down as much as 2% during the day) while the S&P 500 was down 0.3%, after Musk tweeted on 7 Oct blaming Indian 'oligarchs' (naming Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel as making a launch difficult) for blocking Starlink. Starlink is still waiting for satellite spectrum in India. This delays one future market; it does not change current revenue (Starlink operates in 160+ countries).

Deutsche Bank (analyst Edison Yu) estimates 13.5m Starlink consumer subscribers at end-September, up from 12.0m at end-June, with over 370,000 added in September alone; North America 5.5m (41% of the total), +126,000 in September. Starlink Q3 revenue is expected at about $4.8bn vs $4.3bn in Q2 (+12% vs the previous quarter), and Q3 AI revenue is expected to exceed Starlink's for the first time.
evidence.src: Deutsche Bank estimate, quoted by Dow Jones, 8 Oct 2026

past.date: Tue 4 Aug 2026, after the US close (Wed 5 Aug, early morning Singapore)
past.vs: Revenue $7.81bn, +92% vs a year earlier, vs about $6.7-6.9bn expected. EPS -$0.09 vs about -$0.26 to -$0.29 expected. Adjusted EBITDA $3.5bn vs about $2.0bn.
past.guide: No revenue or profit guidance. Capex in each of the next two quarters similar to the June quarter's $18.4bn (about $13bn had been expected). Target: $100bn annualised revenue run-rate by December 2026.
past.reaction: -13.6% on 5 Aug while the Nasdaq-100 fell 0.8%; then +6.1% and +15.8% on 6-7 Aug.
take: Revenue beat everywhere. Connectivity +66% (12.0m Starlink subscribers, double a year earlier), AI +247%, Space +29%, each vs the same quarter a year earlier.
AI turned EBITDA-positive (operating profit before depreciation) on new AI computing agreements: $1.1bn adjusted EBITDA; computing agreements brought in $1.6bn of revenue.
Spending is the problem. Capex $18.4bn in the quarter ($15.8bn of it for AI), 2.35x revenue; free cash flow −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026.

Large cash cushion, but it is being spent fast: $93.5bn cash plus $6.5bn marketable securities at 30 Jun ($100.0bn), against $39.4bn of debt, after a $25bn bond that partly repaid a $20bn bridge loan; backlog $47.5bn. At the H1 pace (−$12.5bn a quarter) that cash lasts about 8 quarters; at capex near $18bn a quarter, closer to 6 (rough estimate, before any new borrowing or share sales).
Space still loss-making (operating loss $542m) while Starship is developed.
New front: plans a mobile network on EchoStar spectrum, competing with phone carriers.
past.impact: Demand strong (DM4a/b/c bullish); no guidance (DM3 blank); cash burn shows in the quality check and chain C3.

chains.name: Share supply (lock-ups)
evidence: No single tranche of 5%+ of shares is due within 20 trading days yet, so the chain reads Quiet; it turns Active about 8 Oct, when the ~1.3bn-share (9.9%) post-results tranche comes within 20 trading days. Meanwhile 328m shares (2.5% of all 13,182m) unlock on 9 Oct and 328m on 24 Oct (a Saturday, so tradable from 26 Oct): 5.0% together (Motley Fool, 16 Aug and 15 Sep).

Next: about 1.3bn shares (9.9%) on the second full trading day after Q3 results; 342m on 8 Dec when the main 180-day lock-up ends (one tracker puts the 8 Dec total at about 798m); Musk's roughly 6.1-6.4bn shares (sources differ; about half of all shares) stay locked until about 14 Jun 2027.
The 911.5m-share release on 6 Aug was absorbed: +6.1% that day (CNN). The 9 Sep release coincided with a 3.9% fall (Motley Fool).

lead: SpaceX's call is Building history (day 8 of 10) while today's zone is Buy, at +38 on a −100 to +100 scale (Buy line +30), up from +36 on 7 Oct because Liquidity rose to +23 from +8 as Fed rate expectations turned bullish (the shares fell 4.19%, and the valuation premium to peers narrowed from +238% to +230%); any call would still be capped at Hold by two quality red flags.
bullets: A reading, but not a call yet. 74% of indicator weight has live data vs the 70% needed (unchanged from 7 Oct; it was 66% on 2 Oct); 8 of the 10 trading days needed are now recorded. Forecast revisions (DM2, 8 of 100 points) show 2027 earnings per share of $2.04 expected today vs $0.68 expected 90 days ago (+201.4%), a big jump from a small base, so treat it with care. Even once confirmed, two quality red flags cap the call at Hold: free cash flow was −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026, and the operating loss was 1.6x the interest bill over the same two quarters.

Demand scores +100, on a thin base. 57% of the Demand weight has live data (the bucket needs 50%). In the June quarter, vs the same quarter a year earlier, Connectivity (Starlink) revenue grew 66%, AI 247% and Space 29%; Google searches for Starlink were 24.4% above the same 4 weeks of 2025 (a noisy measure: the Starship flight fell in that window). Much of the AI jump came from renting out computing capacity, and one AI customer alone was 12.2% of company revenue in the 6 months to June (10-Q).

The price is extreme vs peers. Valuation scores −100: investors pay 100.2x expected profit over the next 12 months vs 30.3x for Iridium, the only space peer with a usable P/E, a one-peer comparison (+230%, down from +238% on 7 Oct); SpaceX's 100x is above the 80x range peers must pass, so the page adds a caution, but it still counts as very expensive. On total company value vs operating profit before depreciation it is 349x vs 8.3x for the median of four peers.

Price trend scores +100, helped by a fall in the peers. The price is 10.8% above its average since listing ($144.94) and 28.8 points ahead of the space peers over 63 trading days: the shares are up 10.5% over that time while the peers fell an average of 18.3%. The shares closed at $160.57, −4.19% on the day vs −1.39% for the Nasdaq-100, 24% below their post-listing high close ($211.40 on 16 Jun) and 19% above the $135 IPO price.

Money flows are neutral. Liquidity scores +23, up from +8 on 7 Oct, because Fed rate expectations turned bullish: markets price a 16% chance of a Fed rate rise at the late-October meeting, down from 34% a month earlier (Polymarket). Buying vs selling volume is neutral (0.92x up-day vs down-day volume, last 20 trading days) and the dollar index is 3.05 points higher than 20 trading days ago. Short interest fell 12.0% vs a month earlier (2.4% of float). Share supply is rising: 656m shares (5.0% of all shares) unlock in October and about 1.3bn (9.9%) just after Q3 results.
defects: Coverage 74% (above the 70% floor); a call is possible once 7 of 10 trading days agree. Forecast revisions (DM2) are live again: the forecast 90 days earlier is now $0.64 a share vs $2.05 today, above the minimum base, though still a small one.
Quality override O3: 2 red flags (free cash flow −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026; operating loss 1.6x interest), so any call is capped at Hold.
VL3 (P/E vs own history) removed: no earnings history yet. To be reinstated when history allows.
Revenue and margin trends (DM1, DM6) blank: too few quarters filed with the SEC.
No company guidance, so DM3 is blank.

Forward P/E vs peers rests on one peer (Iridium): the other seven are loss-making or outside the 2x-80x data-quality range. Yahoo's next-fiscal-year figure is 86.7x; price ÷ the FY2027 consensus of $2.05 gives about 82x. SpaceX's own 104.4x and 364x (EV/EBITDA) are above the 80x range that peers must pass, yet are still scored.
Price trend +100 comes from short-history measures and from peers falling further; the shares rose 10.2% over 63 trading days while the peers fell an average of 16.3%.

Customer concentration and related parties are not scored: one AI customer ('Customer B' in the 10-Q, not named; press reports suggest Anthropic, unconfirmed) was 12.2% of revenue in the 6 months to June, about 19.5% of June-quarter revenue (Unite.AI); another customer was 17.9% across all three segments in the same 6 months. The 10-Q balance sheet shows about $13.3bn of related-party debt at 30 Jun (details in its Note 17, not reviewed here), and Terafab is a joint project with Tesla.
No cash runway line: cash and securities of $100.0bn vs free cash flow of −$25.0bn in 6 months (rough estimate: 6-8 quarters before new funding).
Demand inputs (DM4a/b/c, DM5) are entered by hand from results releases and Google Trends. DM5 (search interest) is a noisy attention measure that jumps on news.
Short interest as % of float (LQ2) and trading volume (LQ1) shift mechanically while lock-ups add tradable shares.
Revenue mix uses short-history mode: only the Jun 2026 10-Q is filed, giving four quarters with a gap (Mar/Jun 2025 and Mar/Jun 2026).

CON.sells: Starlink satellite internet: home and business broadband, aviation, maritime, government (Starshield) and direct-to-phone service.
CON.buyers: Consumers (12.0m subscribers in June 2026), airlines, shipping lines, businesses and governments.
pos: The only profitable part: 38.6% segment operating margin in the Jun 2026 quarter (35.7% a year earlier).
Mostly monthly subscriptions, so revenue recurs.
+66% vs the same quarter a year earlier; subscribers doubled to 12.0m.
neg: Share of sales fell from 64% to 55% (Jun 2025 → Jun 2026 quarter) because AI grew faster.

Revenue per subscriber is lower than a year ago: Connectivity revenue grew 66% while subscribers doubled (roughly −17% per subscriber). Management says average revenue per user held at $66 a month vs the March quarter.
Satellites must be replaced every few years, so capital spending never stops.

AI.sells: xAI: Grok chatbot subscriptions and API, advertising on X, and AI computing agreements (renting out data-centre capacity).
AI.buyers: Consumers and businesses (Grok), advertisers (X), and companies buying AI computing.
pos: +247% vs the same quarter a year earlier; now 33% of sales (18% a year earlier).
New AI computing agreements made the segment EBITDA-positive in the Jun 2026 quarter ($1.1bn adjusted EBITDA; $1.6bn of computing revenue).
neg: Still loses money: segment operating margin −49% in the Jun 2026 quarter (−207% a year earlier).
Takes most of the capital spending: $15.8bn of the $18.4bn capex in the Jun 2026 quarter (86%) was for AI, and management expects a similar level in each of the next two quarters.
Advertising on X is shrinking: $367m vs $426m in the same quarter a year earlier.
Much of the jump came from new computing agreements, and one customer (not named) was 12.2% of company revenue in the 6 months to June; how repeatable these deals are is not yet known.

SPA.sells: Falcon and Starship launches, Dragon crew and cargo flights, and development work for NASA and defence.
SPA.buyers: NASA, the US Space Force and other agencies, commercial satellite operators; it also launches SpaceX's own Starlink satellites.
pos: +29% vs the same quarter a year earlier.
Owning the launcher lets SpaceX put up its own Starlink satellites at cost, which rivals cannot match.
neg: Loss-making while Starship is developed: operating loss $542m in the Jun 2026 quarter (segment margin −56%).
One-off missions, not recurring: revenue swings with launch timing ($619m in the Mar 2026 quarter vs $962m in June).
Smallest part: 12% of sales in the Jun 2026 quarter.

shift.title: What the shift means for SpaceX
pos: Faster growth: revenue +92% vs the same quarter a year earlier (Jun 2026), led by AI (+247%).

Losses narrowed sharply in the June quarter: all segments together earned −1.8% operating margin vs −23.8% a year earlier, helped by the AI computing deals. But the March quarter was −41.4%, and over the half year losses widened: −16.7% (6 months to Jun 2026) vs −11.6% a year earlier.
neg: Less recurring: subscription-based Connectivity fell from 64% to 55% of sales while AI, which relies on newer and less proven deals, rose from 18% to 33%.

Heavy cash burn: the AI build-out needs about $18bn of capital spending a quarter, far above operating cash (free cash flow −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026, against $100.0bn of cash and securities).
Only four quarters of segment data are filed (with a gap), so the trend is short.
The '30.5-point mix drag' line reflects AI's very deep loss a year ago (−207% margin) weighing more now AI is a bigger share; AI's own margin improved to −49%.
